### TAG-221: VHDL emitter: emit callee entities

**Status:** ⬜ Not started

## Software Notes

When a definition's body is an **instance invocation** of another definition — the structural-composition form now supported at the runtime layer ([TAG-218](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-218/runtime-support-top-level-definitions-whose-resolution-is-instance)) — the VHDL emitter produces an instantiation site but no matching entity declaration. GHDL rejects the result with `unit "<callee>" not found in library "work"`.

This is not a runtime bug. `verify_examples` shows all affected examples as `parse: ok` and, where a `.tb.vec` exists, `runtime: ok N/N`. The failure is purely at the emission stage: the callee's entity and architecture are never written into the emitted `.vhd` file, so the `entity work.<callee> port map (...)` line at the invocation site refers to something GHDL can't resolve.

Four examples are currently blocked on this, and the error shape is identical in each:

```
TAG-129  example-12.19.ms.ipl    unit "ms_not"  not found in library "work"
TAG-180  example-12.10.ms.ipl    unit "fanin"   not found in library "work"
TAG-211  example-12.18.ms.ipl    unit "fulladd" not found in library "work"
TAG-218  tag-218.ms.ipl          unit "inner"   not found in library "work"
```

In each case the emitted file *contains* the architecture for the callee — but with a mangled name that GHDL also can't match:

```
[TAG-211] .verify_scratch/TAG-211-example-12.18-bundling.ms.ipl.vhd:236:21:error: entity "fulladd" was not analysed
architecture rtl of fulladd is
```

Note the loop: the instantiation says `entity work.fulladd`, and later the file tries to declare `architecture rtl of fulladd`, but GHDL says neither was ever analyzed. That's the tell that the entity declaration itself (`entity fulladd is ... end fulladd;`) is either missing, syntactically invalid, or emitted after the architecture that references it.

## Repro

Minimal, from [TAG-218](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-218/runtime-support-top-level-definitions-whose-resolution-is-instance):

```
INNER[(A<>)($Y)
  $A
  :
  K[Y<K>]
  L[Y<L>]
]
WRAP[(A<>)($Y)
  INNER($A)(Y<>)
  :
]
```

Emit VHDL and feed it to GHDL:

```
zig build verify
```

The emitted `.verify_scratch/TAG-218-tag-218.ms.ipl.vhd` will contain `entity work.inner port map (a => ..., y => y);` in `WRAP`'s architecture, but no top-level `entity inner` declaration.

## What the fix probably involves

The runtime already has the mirror of this logic. In `rules.zig`, `buildRulesAtDepth` walks `def.resolution` for `.invoke` statements and calls `inlineInvocation`, which resolves the callee via `findDefinition(definitions, inv.name)` and recursively builds its rules. The emitter needs the analogous walk:

1. For every definition being emitted, scan `def.resolution` for `.invoke` statements.
2. Collect the set of unique callee names referenced.
3. For each callee, emit its `entity` + `architecture` **before** the parent's architecture (dependency order, possibly recursive if callees themselves invoke other definitions).
4. Ensure the emitted entity name at the declaration matches exactly what the instantiation site references (`work.<name>`).

Step 3's ordering is the likely culprit for the "was not analysed" cascades — VHDL requires an entity to be declared (or at least analyzed) before any architecture that uses it. If the current emitter writes all architectures first and all entities later, or interleaves them in the wrong order, GHDL will reject even well-formed entities.

## Acceptance criteria

* `verify_examples` shows `ghdl: ok` for [TAG-129](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-129/example-1219-imperative-form-of-expression), [TAG-180](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-180/example-1210-conditional-input-expression), [TAG-211](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-211/example-1218-bundling-digits-into-numbers), and [TAG-218](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-218/runtime-support-top-level-definitions-whose-resolution-is-instance).
* No regressions: every example currently `ghdl: ok` stays `ghdl: ok`.
* The emitted `.vhd` for [TAG-218](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-218/runtime-support-top-level-definitions-whose-resolution-is-instance) (the smallest repro) contains, in order:
  1. `entity inner is ... end inner;`
  2. `architecture rtl of inner is ... end rtl;` (or wherever the callee's body goes)
  3. `entity wrap is ... end wrap;` / `architecture rtl of wrap is ...`
  4. `entity wrap_network` at the top if that's the current emission structure

  The exact order isn't mandated — the requirement is that GHDL accepts the file and every `entity work.X` reference has a matching declaration earlier in the file.

## Scope notes

* This ticket is **independent of** [TAG-220](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-220/value-transformcollectvaluetransformrules-produces-token-input-rules) (`value_transform.collectValueTransformRules` token-input rules). [TAG-220](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-220/value-transformcollectvaluetransformrules-produces-token-input-rules) is a *runtime* bug blocking TAG-211's `runtime:` column; this ticket is an *emitter* bug blocking TAG-211's `ghdl:` column. Both need to land for [TAG-211](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-211/example-1218-bundling-digits-into-numbers) to go fully green, but neither blocks the other.
* [TAG-211](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-211/example-1218-bundling-digits-into-numbers) is currently `⬛ expected fail` overall, and it will remain so until both are fixed. Once both land, its `result` should become `✅ PASS`.
* The four affected examples span three different invocation shapes (single callee with one output, single callee with two outputs, multiple callees with shared intermediate signals). Whatever fix handles [TAG-218](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-218/runtime-support-top-level-definitions-whose-resolution-is-instance) (the simplest) should be checked against [TAG-129](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-129/example-1219-imperative-form-of-expression) (the most complex, 13 invocations) before declaring victory.
* The simulation failures for [TAG-130](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-130/example-121-unnamed-source-place-in-an-invocation) and [TAG-148](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-148/example-1211-controlled-fan-out-expression) (`cannot find entity or configuration example_12_1_tb`) are a **separate** issue — those are testbench entity-name mismatches, not missing callee entities. Don't fold them into this ticket.
